source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the model and serial number of the appliance.
3. Note the make and type of the appliance (e.g., toaster, microwave, etc.).
4. List any visible damage or wear that could affect safety.
5. Document the date and time of the test.
6. Use a standardized checklist to ensure that all relevant safety aspects are checked.
7. Perform inspections according to manufacturer guidelines and corresponding safety regulations.
8. Record readings for electrical continuity, insulation resistance, and earth continuity.
9. Describe any failed safety checks accurately, indicating which specific test failed (e.g., insulation resistance below limit).
10. Take photos of any failed components or areas where the test did not pass.
11. Make explicit the reason(s) for failure (e.g., damaged insulation, faulty earth connection).
12. Date-stamp all test results and supporting documentation.
13. Record the signature of the technician conducting the test for accountability.
14. Log any immediate actions
